subject: Re: Deployment mode & pricing — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Finex)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Singh <anita.singh@finex.com>, Kevin Brooks <kevin.brooks@finex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & pricing — quick recap and next steps

Hi Anita / Kevin —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap from today’s discovery and the asks we agreed on:

Summary of needs (from call)
- Throughput: ~80 req/s average, with occasional peaks to ~150 req/s for batch jobs.
- Latency target: p95 under 350ms for text-generation endpoints.
- Data residency: US-only; SOC 2 required.
- Security: likely need VPC peering and customer-managed keys if we go private.
- Decision drivers: cost predictability, data isolation, and ease of integration with your existing infra.

Deployment modes we discussed
- Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest to go-live, per-token pricing, suitable if data residency and SOC2 are satisfied through our hosted offer.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, monthly/annual commits, lower per-token unit cost at scale.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network control and KMS/HSM integration for regulated workflows — higher upfront and infra ops.

Attachments I shared: redwood-pricing-table-v3.xlsx (high-level cost comps) and mutual-action-plan.docx (MAP). Please review the pricing sheet for the baseline assumptions we used.

Asks / next steps
- Can you confirm the expected sustained qps (you mentioned 80 req/s) and a representative prompt/response token size? This drives the per-token hosted estimate vs. required dedicated capacity.
- Do you have an internal procurement timeline or constraints for committing to reserved capacity?
- Any preference for model family (e.g., smaller open models vs. LLM-equivalent throughput) — we can show both cost vectors.

Proposed follow-up: pricing walk-through with our solutions/finance folks on Thu Mar 12 at 11:00 AM PT. Does that work?

I’ll put together two scenarios for the call: 1) Hosted per-token projection for 80 req/s (with burst headroom), and 2) Dedicated reserved capacity commit with expected unit economics and overage terms. If you’re trending toward private, I’ll add a back-of-envelope for VPC/on-prem lift.

Thanks —

Looping in an initial cost sketch ahead of our Thu call. High-level notes below — will produce line-item numbers in the spreadsheet for the meeting.

Assumptions used
- Sustained: 80 req/s * 1,200 tokens = 96k tokens/s => ~5.76M tokens/min (note: double-check tokenization assumptions; this is text-dense).
- Working hours: 24/7 assumed for baseline; if you run scheduled batch windows we can model lower 24/7 baseline.

Hosted (per-token) sketch
- Per-token price (example): $0.0008 / token for LLM-class generation (placeholder; final depends on model).
- Monthly estimate: 5.76M tokens/min * 60 * 24 * 30 * $0.0008 ≈ $198k/month (ballpark).
- Pros: no infra commitments, fast pilot; Cons: potentially higher costs at scale and less isolation.

Dedicated (reserved capacity) sketch
- Dedicated reserved commit priced as a monthly GPU capacity bundle (example): commit to N GPU-hours or throughput tier. At our mid-tier commit, equivalent unit cost could reduce to ~$0.0002–0.00035 / token when amortized across sustained throughput + caching benefits.
- Typical constructs: monthly/annual commit with defined peak throughput and predictable overage rate (often 1.2x of committed unit price for short bursts).
- Pros: cost predictability and isolation; Cons: requires commit and lead-time to provision.

Private (VPC / on-prem) sketch
- Higher initial setup (networking, KMS integration, on-prem packaging) and minimum commit levels; good fit if data residency + full isolation are mandatory.

Next steps for Thu
- I’ll bring a simple 3-option model in the spreadsheet: hosted PAYG, dedicated 12-month commit, private VPC estimate.
- Please confirm whether the 1,200 token average is representative (samples welcome).

Call highlights

- Preliminary preference: Dedicated for predictability; still want hosted pilot option to validate integration.
- Procurement asked for clear overage rules and early termination language for dedicated commits.

Agreed MAP (next actions)

- Finex (Anita / Kevin): share a representative prompt set or 3–5 example requests (anonymized) so we can refine tokenization and cost math.
- Procurement (procurement@finex.com): share preferred contracting cadence / procurement constraints for reserved commits.

Seller notes / risks
- If actual average token counts are materially higher than 1,200, hosted costs grow linearly; dedicated economics improve.
- Private VPC lead time: ~6–8 weeks for network and KMS integration once contract is signed.

Next meeting: Pricing review on Mon Mar 16 (we’ll propose times early tomorrow). Please reply with any calendar conflicts.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you a clean compare and recommendation.
